thread.title: FAANGs On the Verge of Bear Market, Is the Trade 'Dead'? | Investopedia

author: investopedia.com
title: FAANGs On the Verge of Bear Market, Is the Trade 'Dead'? | Investopedia

organizations.name: correction territory stock off 52-week high facebook

text:
Recent market turbulence, driven by a myriad of factors including fears over heightened global trade tensions, rising interest rates, and broader geopolitical instability, have taken a bite out of some of 2017's highest flying tech stocks, particularly international tech behemoths known as the FAANG stocks. FAANG is an acronym for the market's five leading tech stocks, Facebook Inc. ( FB ), Apple Inc. ( AAPL ), Amazon ( AMZN ), Netflix ( NFLX ), and Alphabet Inc.'s Google ( GOOGL ).
Earlier this year, Apple Inc. and Amazon.com Inc. became the first U.S. corporations to surpass $1 trillion in market capitalization, but the companies are now more than $100 billion and $200 billion away from that threshold, respectively. Facebook Inc., Netflix Inc., and Alphabet Inc. have also faced significant downward pressure.
FAANG Stocks Fall into Correction Territory
Stock Off 52-Week High Facebook 34.5% Apple 18.6% Amazon 20.2% Netflix 32.7% Alphabet 19.1% S&P 7.2% 'No Leadership Anymore in the Stock Market,' Says Chief Investment Officer In an interview with CNBC on Tuesday, Bleakley Advisory Group's Peter Boockvar forecasted more declines ahead for equities now that the tech giants are no longer carrying the market.
"Collectively, there's no question that [the FAANG] trade is dead," the Chief Investment Officer said. “Taken together, there's really no leadership anymore in the stock market."
Boockvar pointed to Facebook's disappointing Q2 results as the start of the downturn, which led the company to lose nearly a quarter of its value. Apple's mixed Q4 results spooked investors further, with bears fearing that the company cannot shift fast enough away from a decelerating hardware business to software and services. Meanwhile, Amazon has had a tough time justifying its lofty valuation and sustaining its top-line growth amid heightened competition.
Boockvar expects FAANG weakness to couple with larger market headwinds and extend to other sectors, as we saw with the market's leading semiconductor companies last week.
"So, each of these stocks, going forward, are going to trade on their own footing and not as a group," Boockvar said.
Not all are so bearish on FAANG's future, yet the general consensus on the Street seems to be that investors are better off scrutinizing each company individually rather than betting on them as a group.
In response to Amazon falling into correction territory on Monday, for example, Nomura Instinet analysts issued a note recommending that investors buy the stock at a discount. Bulls cited the Seattle-based retailer's booming profitability and wrote that Amazon's sales and gross profit dollars are growing faster than its ability to spend.
